raw_response:
Alright, let me think about this year's cotton...

I've been on this land forty years, same ten mu of cotton my whole life near enough. Just me and the old lady in the house now — kids moved away. So I plant cotton like always. My neighbors all grow cotton here in our village, we all do about the same.

**Seed.** I go down to the supply shop in town before planting and buy cotton seed, whatever they have — the same kind Old Wang and the others buy. About 50 yuan a mu. I don't save my own seed anymore, the new seed does better.

**Ground preparation.** End of March I rent the small tractor from my nephew to plow up the field. Costs me about 50-60 yuan a mu. Before the last pass I spread one bag of compound fertilizer per mu — the 15-15-15 stuff, 50 kg a bag. That's my base fertilizer. About 150 yuan a bag these days, prices keep going up.

**Planting.** Around April 20, when the ground's warm enough. Me and the wife plant by hand in rows, takes us four or five days to do the ten mu. Cover with plastic mulch on some of it — helps keep the moisture in early on.

**Topdressing.** When the cotton starts flowering, end of June, I put one bag of urea per mu — that's 40-some kg. Pushes it along when it's setting bolls. Maybe 100 yuan a bag.

**Irrigation.** I've got the well share with two other households. I water twice usually — once right after planting if it hasn't rained, and once in July when the bolls are setting. Pumping costs money, the electric meter runs. If it rains enough I skip one. Don't water unless the leaves start curling.

**Pesticide.** Cotton is nothing but trouble with bugs. Bollworm, aphids, red spider in the hot weather. I spray every couple weeks through summer, maybe five or six times total. Whatever my neighbor Wang is using I use — he keeps up with what works. Mix it myself with the backpack sprayer.

**Picking.** This is the hard part. Starts early September, goes through to end of October, three or four picks. With just me and the wife for ten mu we can't get it all done fast enough, so I hire four or five women from the village for about ten days at the peak — 100 yuan a day each now, used to be 60. Picking has gotten expensive.

**Yield.** My land's alright, not the best but not bad. Usually I get around 250 kg of lint per mu, some years 280 when weather's good, one bad year with the bollworm I got barely 180. I figure 250 this year if nothing goes wrong.

Cash is always tight. Cotton price isn't what it used to be either. But I know cotton — at my age I'm not going to start learning something new.
